title: Officially support bootstrap.run
body:
### Checklist

- [x] I have searched the [existing issues](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues) for similar feature requests.
- [x] I added a descriptive title and summary to this issue.

### Summary

Hi,

Streamlit supports running the app via cli streamlit run your_app.py

I request bootstrap.run to be supported, and documented, so it can run within python.
so streamlit apps can be distributed standalone with frameworks like nuitka.


from streamlit import config as _config
from streamlit.web.bootstrap import run
_config.set_option("server.headless", True)
run('your_app.py', args=[], flag_options=[], is_hello=False)

But method run it’s not stable, nor documented.
It’s an internal method

Thank you,
Robert

## Update

Streamlit 1.59 introduces an officially supported alternative to calling the internal `streamlit.web.bootstrap.run` API directly.

The new public API is:

```python
import streamlit as st

app = st.App("your_app.py")

if __name__ == "__main__":
    app.run()
```

`App.run()` starts a local Streamlit server for the app and supports programmatic config overrides:

```python
app.run(config={"server.headless": True, "server.port": 8502})
```

So instead of documenting `bootstrap.run` as a stable public API, we now have a supported public entry point for launching an `st.App` from Python code. This is planned to ship in Streamlit 1.59.
